translation:
Jaisalmer

_Gurjar khandme pragate, Gyani Gorakhnath ||_
_Das Kabir Jivana, mastak dino hath ||129|| Prabodh_
(In the Gurjar land there manifested the wise Gorakhnath; the servant Kabir, Jivana, laid his hand upon his head.)

Jivandasji Maharaj says that when the yogi Gorakhnath manifested as Gyaniji in the region of Gujarat, the devotee Kabir showed him grace, gave him his blessing, granted him devotion to God, and thereby delivered him.

Gorakhnath went to Kabir to display the power of his eighty-four siddhis (occult powers), and, sitting atop his trident, began calling Kabir to come and converse with him. Then Kabir took one end of a ball of thread, kept it on the ground, threw the ball into the sky, and sat down upon its upper end, saying, "Come and sit facing me, then we shall talk." In this way Gorakh's pride was broken. He therefore went to Kabir's refuge and asked for devotion. Kabir said, "You have spent this incarnation chasing after siddhis (occult powers); therefore I shall give you devotion only in another incarnation." So this Gorakh took birth in Jaisalmer in a royal household, and his name was Chaturasingh.

Although Chaturasingh reached a marriageable age, he refused to marry. So, by persuading and coaxing him, they set about marrying him to a girl named Ganga, daughter of the king of Jodhpur; but he fled from the wedding canopy (chori) and, going to Jaipur, took initiation from Krishnadas Payahari, and performed austerities for fourteen years at Shulpaneshwar. Searching for him, four soldiers came bringing Gangaba (Ganga) along, and began entreating him to return. But Krishnadas Payahari had given this Chaturasingh the name "Gyani" (the wise one), and this Gyaniji gave the soldiers such teaching that all four of them became fakirs. One of these soldiers stayed at Bavaghor, where his grave is; the grave of another soldier is near Fatehpura in Vadodara. (That grave was destroyed in the communal riots of 2005 CE; it has since been rebuilt.) Thus Gyaniji set up a household with Gangaba; their samadhi (tomb-shrine) and descendants are alive today near Mota Sanja, Jhagadia. In this way, Jaisalmer, being the birthplace of Gyaniji Maharaj, is a sacred site as the birthplace of our guru.

It is written in the file of papers of Nazar's research — in the paper it is written — that the spring bearing Jivanji Maharaj's name, the living spring of water, is at Gyaniji's shrine (at Mota Sanja).
